subject: POC charter & evaluation playbook — next steps and kickoff
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@zenbyte.ai>, Rahul Singh <rahul@zenbyte.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: POC charter & evaluation playbook — notes and proposed scope

Hi Elena / Rahul,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise recap of the pain, goals, and a proposed POC scope so we can lock the kickoff and owners. If this aligns, I’ll share calendar invites and the artifact links.

Key pain points you described:
- Erratic response quality for customer-facing chat that needs consistent tone across product lines.
- High per-call cost on current deployment (spiky load with several bursty peaks).
- Platform telemetry gaps: hard to correlate prompt changes with metric regressions.

Business goals for the POC (what success looks like)
- Reduce high-severity quality regressions by 40% (measured by manual evals + automated heuristics).
- Lower per-1000-token inference cost by at least 20% while meeting a 250ms median latency target.
- Prove a repeatable rollout path (canary -> full) with traceable prompt/regression alerts.

Proposed pilot scope (4 weeks) — deliverables and owners
- Week 0 (access/setup): credentials + sample data ingestion; owner: ZenByte infra (Rahul).
- Week 1: Baseline collection — capture 7 days of traffic and run initial evals; owner: Diego / Ben.
- Week 2: Model configuration and quantization experiments; owner: Redwood infra (Ben).
- Week 3: Controlled rollout (canary) + latency/cost optimization; owner: Marissa.
- Week 4: Final evaluation, regression analysis, and SLO handoff doc; owner: Diego.

Success metrics (we’ll instrument these in the pilot):
- Quality: human eval pass-rate and automated semantic-similarity score (target +40% improvement over baseline for flagged cases).
- Cost: per-1k tokens unit cost reduction (target -20%).
- Latency: median tail under 250ms and 95th < 600ms.
- Reliability: <1% request error rate during controlled load tests.

Access and setup items we need from ZenByte this week:
1) S3/secure drop with 7–14 days of anonymized chat logs (sample row schema in the attached CSV).
2) A read-only API key for your staging environment and the name/IP for allowed hosts (we’ll provide our SSH key if you prefer SFTP).
3) List of top 200 prompt variations and any current prompt-engineering rulesheets.
4) Contact for procurement so we can exchange a standard SOW (cc procurement if needed).

Attachments: zenbyte_poc_charter_v1.pdf (POC charter), sample_prompt_set_v3.csv (sample prompt rows + annotator guidance).

Proposed kickoff: Wednesday, Jan 27 at 10:00 AM PT — 45 minutes. If that works for your team we’ll send invites and a short agenda.

Next steps (from our side):
- I’ll publish the POC charter + evaluation playbook to the shared Drive link and open a HubSpot deal task for onboarding.
- Ben will prep a short checklist for infra access to reduce friction.

If any of the scope or metrics above don’t match what you expected, flag them directly and we’ll adjust before kickoff.

Thanks,

Diego Fernandez
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Great, thanks Elena — helpful questions. Quick replies inline and next actions below.

1) Human eval rubric: we’ll use a 3-point scale (Acceptable / Needs Edit / Fail) with examples for each severity bucket. I’ll attach the rubric and a short annotation guide with the next email. That rubric is what we reference for the +40% target (focused on cases currently flagged as Fail).

2) Cost assumptions: our baseline assumes 1) average batch size of 8 for interactive queries, 2) KV/prefix caching for repeat prompts, and 3) quantized model variant (we’ll run 8-bit experiments in Week 2). If you have a different average batch size, tell us and Ben will re-run the cost model.

3) Owners & timeline: shifting Week 0 infra coordination to you (Elena) is fine — thanks for helping unblock Rahul’s schedule. We’ll keep Rahul in loop for credentials and final sign-off.

Immediate next actions (from Redwood):
- Marissa will send a calendar invite for Jan 27 kickoff and include a short agenda (we’ll propose both 10 AM PT and 1 PM PT as alternatives).
- Ben will prepare the infra access checklist and a minimal runbook for staging keys.
- I’ll attach the human-eval rubric and a sample scoring sheet in a follow-up.

If Procurement sends the SOW, we’ll review and return edits within 48 hours.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Diego
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
